lessons.title: Pre-cleaning Equipment and Operations
lessons.body: Pre-cleaning removes straw, leaves, empty grains, and dirt before paddy enters the mill. In Africa, most small mills use a combination of a vibrating screen and a destoner. The vibrating screen has two or three layers with different hole sizes: top layer 10-12 mm for large trash, middle layer 5-6 mm for smaller trash, and bottom layer 2-3 mm for sand. A fan blows light materials away. For a 1-ton-per-hour mill, the screen area should be at least 1.5 square meters. The screen angle is usually 10-15 degrees, and the vibration speed is 300-400 rpm. Feed paddy evenly using a hopper with a gate; uneven feeding reduces efficiency. Check screens daily for holes or tears; replace worn screens immediately. Clean the machine after every 8 hours of operation. In rural areas, pre-cleaning can also be done manually with a sieve or winnowing, but this is slow and less effective. A simple motorized pre-cleaner costs about $500-$1,500 and pays for itself by reducing wear on downstream equipment. Always wear a dust mask when cleaning the machine. After pre-cleaning, paddy should have less than 1% foreign matter. Test by taking a 1 kg sample and hand-sorting. If trash exceeds 1%, adjust the screen or feed rate. Pre-cleaning also removes stones larger than 5 mm, but smaller stones need a destoner. Remember: pre-cleaning protects your husker and polisher from damage and improves rice quality. In West Africa, many mills skip pre-cleaning and suffer frequent breakdowns. Don't be that mill. Invest in a good pre-cleaner and maintain it daily.

lessons.title: De-stoning and Magnetic Separation
lessons.body: De-stoning removes stones and heavy particles that can damage the husker and end up in final rice. A destoner works by fluidizing a bed of paddy on a vibrating deck while air blows upward. Stones, being heavier, sink and move up the inclined deck, while paddy floats and moves down. The deck angle is typically 5-10 degrees, and vibration is 400-600 rpm. Air velocity must be adjusted so paddy just fluidizes; too much air blows paddy away, too little lets stones stay mixed. For a 1-ton-per-hour mill, the destoner deck should be about 1 meter wide and 1.5 meters long. Feed paddy at a constant rate; sudden surges reduce separation. Check the stone discharge outlet every 30 minutes to ensure stones are being removed. Magnetic separation uses magnets to remove iron particles like nails, wire, and screws. Install a permanent magnet or electromagnet in the chute before the husker. A good magnet can catch particles as small as 0.5 mm. Clean the magnet every 4 hours; iron buildup reduces its strength. In Africa, many mills use a simple bar magnet mounted at an angle. Test magnetic strength with a small nail; if it doesn't stick, replace the magnet. After de-stoning and magnetic separation, paddy should have less than 0.1% stones and zero iron particles. Take a 1 kg sample and check by hand. If stones remain, reduce feed rate or increase air. If iron remains, add a second magnet. These steps are critical because a single stone can break a husker rubber roll, costing $50-$200 to replace. A nail can spark and cause a fire. So always run de-stoning and magnetic separation before husking.

lessons.title: Paddy Husking and Separation
lessons.body: Husking removes the outer hull from paddy to produce brown rice. In Africa, most small mills use a rubber roll husker. Two rubber rolls spin in opposite directions at different speeds: one fast (about 1000 rpm) and one slow (about 800 rpm). The speed difference creates a shearing action that pulls the hull off. The gap between rolls is critical: too wide and paddy passes unhusked; too narrow and grains break. Set the gap to about 0.5-0.8 mm for long grain, 0.4-0.6 mm for short grain. Adjust while running: feed a handful of paddy and check the output. You want at least 90% husked with less than 5% broken. After husking, a separator separates brown rice from unhulled paddy and hulls. The mixture goes over a vibrating screen with holes sized to let brown rice through but retain unhulled paddy. Unhulled paddy is returned to the husker. Hulls are blown away by a fan and can be used for fuel or animal bedding. For a 1-ton-per-hour mill, the husker needs a 5-7.5 kW motor. Rubber rolls wear out after 80-120 hours of operation; replace them when the surface becomes smooth or cracked. In rural areas, some use a steel huller, but it breaks more grains. Rubber rolls are better for quality. After husking, brown rice should have less than 2% unhulled paddy. Check by taking a 100 g sample. If unhulled paddy is high, narrow the roll gap slightly. If broken grains are high, widen the gap. Always keep the husker clean and lubricated. A well-adjusted husker saves money and produces better rice.

lessons.title: Paddy Drying and Tempering
lessons.body: Paddy must be dried to 12-14% moisture before milling to prevent broken grains and mold. In Africa, sun drying is common: spread paddy in a thin layer (5-10 cm) on a concrete floor or tarpaulin. Stir every 30 minutes. On a sunny day, it takes 1-2 days to dry from 20% to 14%. Use a moisture meter to check; if you don't have one, bite a grain: it should be hard but not shatter. For larger quantities, use a mechanical dryer. A batch dryer with a 1-ton capacity costs about $2,000-$5,000. Set drying air temperature to 40-45Â°C for seed paddy, 50-60Â°C for milling paddy. Higher temperatures cause cracks. Drying too fast also causes cracks; aim for a drying rate of 0.5-1% moisture per hour. After drying, temper paddy by letting it rest in a bin for 12-24 hours. Tempering allows moisture inside the grain to equalize, reducing stress and breakage during milling. During tempering, keep paddy covered to prevent re-wetting. In humid regions, use a fan to circulate air. After tempering, check moisture again; it should be uniform. If you skip tempering, broken grains can increase by 10-20%. In West Africa, many farmers dry on roadsides, which contaminates paddy with sand and stones. Instead, use a clean tarp or concrete floor. Never dry on bare ground. Also, avoid drying on very hot surfaces like metal roofs; they can overheat the grain. For storage, paddy should be at 12-13% moisture. If it's higher, continue drying. Remember: proper drying and tempering are the most important steps for high milling yield. A 1% reduction in broken grains means 1% more head rice, which is money in your pocket.

lessons.title: Storage and Aeration of Paddy
lessons.body: After drying and tempering, store paddy in clean, dry, airtight containers. In Africa, use jute bags, plastic silos, or metal bins. Avoid storing in open piles; rats, insects, and moisture will ruin it. For a small mill, a 5-ton capacity metal silo costs about $1,000-$2,000. Before storing, clean the store and spray with insecticide like Actellic. Place bags on pallets 10 cm off the floor and 30 cm away from walls. Stack bags no more than 10 high to prevent crushing. For bulk storage, fill silos to 80% capacity to allow air circulation. Aeration uses fans to push air through the grain mass to control temperature and moisture. In hot climates, grain can heat up due to respiration. Install aeration ducts at the bottom of the silo and a fan on top. Run the fan when grain temperature exceeds 30Â°C or when moisture is above 13%. Aeration for 1-2 hours per day is usually enough. Check temperature weekly using a probe. If temperature rises above 35Â°C, aerate immediately; otherwise mold and insects thrive. Also check moisture monthly; if it increases, re-dry. In humid areas, store paddy at 12% moisture or less. Use hermetic bags like GrainPro for small quantities; they block oxygen and kill insects without chemicals. A 100 kg hermetic bag costs about $10. For long-term storage (6-12 months), keep paddy at 12% moisture and below 25Â°C. Inspect monthly for insects, rodents, and leaks. Fumigate with phosphine tablets if insects are found. Always follow safety instructions. Proper storage preserves quality and reduces losses. In Africa, post-harvest losses can be 10-20%; good storage cuts that to less than 5%.

lessons.title: Quality Control at Pre-Milling Stage
lessons.body: Quality control at pre-milling ensures paddy is clean, dry, and free of defects before husking. Start with sampling: take 1 kg from every 100 kg lot. Test moisture with a meter; it should be 12-14%. If not, dry or temper again. Check foreign matter by hand-sorting: stones, sand, straw, and metal should be less than 1%. Use a sieve to separate smaller particles. Check for discolored or damaged grains: they should be less than 2%. Discolored grains indicate mold or heat damage; they lower rice quality. Also check for insect damage: look for holes or live insects. If found, fumigate or reject the lot. Test husking potential: take 100 g sample, husk with a small hand husker, and calculate husking ratio. A good lot gives 80-85% brown rice. If less, adjust husker or reject. Check for red rice or other varieties; they reduce market value. Red rice should be less than 0.5%. For seed paddy, test germination: at least 80% should sprout. Keep records of all tests: date, lot number, moisture, foreign matter, and results. This helps trace problems. In Africa, many mills skip quality control and suffer poor yields. A simple quality control kit costs about $200 and includes a moisture meter, sieves, and a hand husker. Train one worker as quality controller. Reject any lot that fails moisture or foreign matter. Remember: garbage in, garbage out. Good pre-milling quality control leads to higher head rice yield, better prices, and happy customers. Do it every day, every lot.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of pre-cleaning paddy?
options: A) To remove stones and iron
B) To remove straw, leaves, and dirt
quiz.explanation: Pre-cleaning removes light trash like straw and leaves before de-stoning.

quiz.q: What is the recommended screen angle for a vibrating pre-cleaner?
quiz.explanation: A 10-15 degree angle allows proper movement of paddy over the screen.

quiz.q: After pre-cleaning, foreign matter should be less than:
quiz.explanation: Pre-cleaning should reduce foreign matter to below 1%.

quiz.q: How often should you clean a pre-cleaner machine?
quiz.explanation: Daily cleaning after 8 hours keeps the machine efficient.

quiz.q: What is the function of a destoner?
options: B) Remove stones and heavy particles
quiz.explanation: Destoners separate stones from paddy by density.

quiz.q: What is the typical deck angle for a destoner?
quiz.explanation: A 5-10 degree incline helps stones move upward while paddy moves downward.

quiz.q: How often should you clean a magnet in magnetic separation?
quiz.explanation: Cleaning every 4 hours prevents iron buildup from reducing magnet strength.

quiz.q: After de-stoning, stones should be less than:
quiz.explanation: Good de-stoning leaves less than 0.1% stones.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of magnetic separation?
quiz.explanation: Magnets catch nails, wire, and other iron pieces.

quiz.q: What is the recommended speed difference between rubber rolls in a husker?
options: B) Fast roll 1000 rpm, slow roll 800 rpm
C) Fast roll 1500 rpm, slow roll 1000 rpm
D) Fast roll 800 rpm, slow roll 1000 rpm
quiz.explanation: A speed difference of about 200 rpm creates shearing action.

quiz.q: What gap between husker rolls is good for long grain paddy?
quiz.explanation: 0.5-0.8 mm is typical for long grain to avoid breakage.

quiz.q: After husking, unhulled paddy should be less than:
quiz.explanation: A good husker leaves less than 2% unhulled paddy.

quiz.q: How often should rubber rolls be replaced?
quiz.explanation: Rubber rolls wear out after 80-120 hours of operation.

quiz.q: What is the ideal moisture content for milling paddy?
quiz.explanation: 12-14% moisture prevents broken grains and mold.

quiz.q: What is tempering in paddy processing?
options: B) Letting paddy rest to equalize moisture
quiz.explanation: Tempering allows moisture inside the grain to equalize, reducing stress.

quiz.q: How long should paddy be tempered after drying?
quiz.explanation: 12-24 hours of tempering is typical.

quiz.q: What is the maximum drying air temperature for milling paddy?
quiz.explanation: 50-60Â°C is safe for milling paddy; higher causes cracks.

quiz.q: Why should paddy not be dried on bare ground?
options: B) It gets contaminated with sand and stones
quiz.explanation: Bare ground adds dirt and stones, reducing quality.

quiz.q: What is the recommended moisture content for storing paddy?
quiz.explanation: 12-13% moisture prevents mold and insect growth.

quiz.q: How should bags of paddy be stacked in storage?
options: A) On the floor, against walls
B) On pallets, 30 cm from walls
C) In the middle of the room
quiz.explanation: Pallets and spacing allow air circulation and prevent moisture.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of aeration in paddy storage?
options: B) To control temperature and moisture
quiz.explanation: Aeration prevents heating and mold by circulating air.

quiz.q: When should aeration fans be run?
quiz.explanation: Run fans when temperature is above 30Â°C or moisture above 13%.

quiz.q: What is a hermetic storage bag?
options: A) A bag that allows air
B) A bag that blocks oxygen
C) A bag made of jute
quiz.explanation: Hermetic bags block oxygen, killing insects without chemicals.

quiz.q: How often should stored paddy be inspected?
quiz.explanation: Monthly inspection catches problems early.

quiz.q: What is the acceptable level of foreign matter at pre-milling quality control?
quiz.explanation: Foreign matter should be below 1% for good milling.

quiz.q: What is the acceptable level of discolored grains?
quiz.explanation: Discolored grains should be less than 2% to maintain quality.

quiz.q: What is a good husking ratio for brown rice?
quiz.explanation: 80-85% brown rice yield indicates good husking.

quiz.q: What should be the maximum red rice content?
quiz.explanation: Red rice should be less than 0.5% to meet market standards.

quiz.q: Why is quality control important at pre-milling?
options: A) It increases yield and quality
C) It is required by law
quiz.explanation: Good quality control leads to higher head rice yield and better prices.

quiz.q: What simple tool can test husking potential?
quiz.explanation: A hand husker can husk a small sample to check husking ratio.
